title: A centralised issuer conduit is modelled as a rate-limited transfer to a deposit address
content:
The Paxos instance converts USDC into PYUSD through the issuer rather than through a market. Its identifiers replace the usual `Token` slot with `Token to Receive`: PYUSD (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.12.1.2.1.4). Its contract addresses list USDC as both `Token Address` and `Underlying Asset Address` (.12.1.2.2.1/.2) plus a `Paxos Deposit Address` `0xFb1F749024b4544c425f5CAf6641959da31EdF37` (.12.1.2.2.3). Its rate limits cover neither inflow nor outflow but "this conduit's transferAssets operations": `maxAmount` 5,000,000 USDC, `slope` 50,000,000 USDC per day (.12.1.2.4.1).

On-chain, the entire operation is a transfer to an address. There is no protocol to call, no receipt token to hold, no redemption function — Spark sends USDC and, by a separate off-chain process at Paxos, receives PYUSD. The `Underlying Asset Address` equalling the `Token Address` is the schema degenerating gracefully: there is no wrapper, only the asset being sent.

What the single `transferAssets` limit therefore bounds is the amount Spark can put at issuer risk per day. Between the transfer and the mint, the position is an unsecured claim on Paxos with no on-chain representation, so the rate limit is not throttling exposure to a protocol but pacing settlement with a company.

Registering this alongside Aave and Uniswap in one tree is the same unification seen with the savings products: one inventory of every route value can take. It does mean the `Active` set mixes venues whose failure mode is a smart-contract bug with one whose failure mode is a counterparty declining to mint, and only the parameter shape — a lone transferAssets limit and a deposit address — signals which is which.
description: The USDC-to-PYUSD Paxos instance replaces Token with Token to Receive, records a Paxos Deposit Address, and its only limit governs transferAssets — the return leg happens off-chain entirely.
